title: Finance Playbook: Budgeting & Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition & Billing
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard processes and operational rules for: budgeting and rolling forecasts, contracts and legal intake, procurement approvals and preferred vendors, and revenue recognition and billing policies. It is intended for finance, product, legal, procurement, and engineering managers who need consistent guidance for planning, committing spend, and recognizing revenue.

Scope

- Budgeting and forecasting (annual budget cadence, rolling forecast, reforecast triggers)
- Contracts and legal intake (contract lifecycle, standard terms, playbook for non-standard terms)
- Procurement procedures (purchase approvals, vendor onboarding, capex vs opex rules)
- Revenue recognition & billing (SaaS usage-based billing, reserved capacity recognition, deferred revenue handling)

Principles

- Accuracy with pragmatism: strive for forecast accuracy while minimizing overhead for teams.
- Centralized approvals for legal/financial risk above thresholds.
- Ownership: finance owns budget consolidation and revenue recognition; product/eng own cost drivers and forecasts for their areas.
- Auditability: all procurement and contract decisions should leave a documented trail (Confluence page + ProcureDesk record).

Owners & Roles

- Finance (Controller): overall ownership of budgeting, forecasts, revenue recognition policies.
- FP&A: budget consolidation, rolling forecasts, variance analysis.
- Legal: contract review, exceptions, master services agreement (MSA) custody.
- Procurement (Ops): vendor onboarding, PO issuance, preferred vendor list.
- Product/Engineering Managers: submit budgets, forecast updates, and provide consumption patterns for usage-based revenue/expenses.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting

Overview
Annual budgeting is the primary planning vehicle for the coming fiscal year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). Rolling forecasts (12-month, updated monthly) provide continuous alignment between committed budgets and expected results.

Cadence & Key Dates

1. Budget kickoff: first week of September.
2. First draft due from teams: October 15.
3. Finance review and iteration: Oct 16 - Nov 15.
4. Executive review: late November.
5. Board submission: early December.
6. Budget effective date: Jan 1.

Forecasting

- Rolling 12-month forecasts updated monthly.
- Reforecast (ad-hoc) required when a variance > 5% of run-rate ARR or when headcount changes by > 3 FTEs in a team.
- Expectations from teams: updated revenue drivers, usage forecasts (tokens, embeddings, reserved capacity commitments), headcount plans, expected major procurement.

Budget Templates & Inputs

Teams must use the canonical FP&A template stored at /confluence/finance-and-legal/templates/budget-template-2026.xlsx. Key input items:
- Headcount plan (role, ramp date, fully-burdened cost)
- Infrastructure (GPU hours, committed capacity, cloud egress)
- COGS drivers (model hosting, third-party APIs)
- Go-to-market spend (ads, events, sales commissions)

Acceptance Criteria

- Each team must reconcile headcount to Workday and capital requests to procurement POs.
- Capital requests > $50k require CFO approval and procurement review.

2) Contracts & Legal Intake

Contract Types Covered

- Customer MSAs and SOWs
- Partner agreements and reseller contracts
- Vendor agreements (cloud, tooling, professional services)
- NDAs and data processing agreements (DPA)

Standard Process

1. Intake: Use Contract Intake form (Confluence link /forms/contract-intake) and attach proposed redlines.
2. Triage: Legal triages by risk level (Low/Medium/High) within 3 business days.
3. Review: Legal + Finance perform review for financial/risk terms (payment terms, indemnity, liability cap, data/security clauses).
4. Approval: Contracts with financial obligations > $100k or unusual indemnity require CFO and GC sign-off.
5. Execution: Legal executes via approved e-sign tool (DocuSign).

Common Negotiation Thresholds (escalation rules)

- Payment terms: Standard is Net 30 for vendors; Net 45 for customers requires Finance approval.
- Liability cap: Standard is liability cap equal to fees paid in last 12 months. Exceptions must be documented and approved by GC.
- Data processing / privacy: Any customer request to host data outside approved regions must be escalated to Security & Compliance.

Templates & Approved Clauses

- Standard MSA: /confluence/finance-and-legal/templates/msa-standard-2025.docx
- DPA template: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-protection/dpa-template-2024.docx

3) Procurement Procedures

Procurement thresholds & approvals

- <= $5k: Team lead approval (recorded in ProcureDesk).
- $5k - $50k: Department head + Procurement approval.
- > $50k (operational) or > $50k capex: Procurement + Finance (FP&A) + CFO sign-off.
- Any multi-year commitment or contract with auto-renewal requires Legal and Procurement review before signature.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist

- Completed vendor request form (ProcureDesk)
- Approved PO or contract
- W-9 or appropriate tax docs (for US vendors)
- Security questionnaire completed: vendors handling sensitive data must complete Security vendor assessment and be listed in vendor registry.
- Bank details verified via Procurement for ACH.

Preferred Vendors & Discounting

- Procurement maintains a preferred vendor list with negotiated discounts (see /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/preferred-vendors-2026).
- Teams should route purchases through preferred vendors where available.

PO & Invoice Flow (step-by-step)

1. Team submits procurement request in ProcureDesk with estimated budget code.
2. Procurement issues PO.
3. Vendor delivers goods/services and submits invoice referencing PO.
4. Accounts Payable matches invoice to PO and approves payment per payment terms.

Example CLI for Procurement Lookup (internal tool)

# look up PO status
procurectl po status --po 2026-PR-0123

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy

Principles

- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, transaction price, allocate price, and recognize when performance obligations are satisfied.
- Billing may be usage-based (hosted API per-token), subscription (reserved capacity), or professional services (SOW).

Customer Billing Models

- Hosted API (usage): Invoiced monthly in arrears; recognized as revenue in the period the usage occurred (measurement: tokens/embeddings).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Upfront or monthly billed. If prepaid for future periods, recognize as deferred revenue and amortize over service period.
- Private (on-prem/license): License revenue recognized based on delivery and rights transferred per contract; maintenance recognized ratably.
- Professional services: Recognize based on milestone completion or percentage-of-completion if measurable.

Deferred Revenue & Billing Examples

Table: Common Scenarios

| Scenario | Billing Timing | Recognition Treatment | Accounting Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Monthly API usage invoice (March invoice for Feb usage) | Invoice Mar 10 | Recognize Feb revenue (accrual) | Revenue Operations / Accounting |
| Annual prepaid dedicated capacity purchased Jan 1 for $120k | Invoice Jan 1 | Defer $120k, recognize $10k monthly | Accounting |
| Multi-year SaaS agreement with installation fee | Install fee billed at start | Allocate to services vs. license; recognize per ASC 606 allocation | Accounting + Legal |

Invoicing & Collection

- Standard invoice terms: Net 30 for customers unless otherwise approved.
- Late payment escalation: reminder at +7d, second notice +30d, account review +60d; Sales & Customer Success notified at +45d.
- Chargebacks and disputes: Customer disputes flagged in Zendesk billing queue; Revenue Operations investigates and issues credit memos if required.

Tax & International Considerations

- VAT/GST: Apply taxes as required by customer billing address. Finance collects VAT registration details for EU customers and ensures correct tax handling in billing system.
- Withholding tax: For cross-border services, coordinate with Legal & Tax to determine withholding obligations.

Reporting & Controls

- Monthly close checklist includes revenue recognition review, deferred revenue rollforward, and a reconciliation of AR ledger to billing system.
- Segregation of duties: billing setup and payment approval are separate roles.
- Audit evidence: maintain contract copies, order confirmations, and invoices in the contract repository for audit.

Appendices

A. Quick Decision Matrix (when to escalate)

- Contract financial obligation > $100k: escalate to CFO & GC.
- Liability cap > standard: escalate to GC.
- Procurement > $50k: CFO approval.
- Forecast variance > 5% run-rate: FP&A reforecast required.
